title: Bind git correlation engine through the bridge
description:
Bind bv's `pkg/correlation` through the engine bridge so bvx can link beads to
commits.

The engine work is mostly exposure rather than new logic — bv already scores
links by explicit reference, co-commit pattern, file overlap and temporal
proximity, and maintains incremental per-commit disk caches.

**Scope**

- New bridge methods: `history`, `causality`, `file_beads`, `file_hotspots`,
  `file_relations`, `orphans`, `related`, `impact_network`
- Swift models for the correlation payloads
- Confidence scores surfaced, never rounded away

**Watch out**

`pkg/correlation/gitcmd.go` shells out to `git`, which the App Sandbox forbids.
Route the sandboxed app through direct object-store reads; the CLI can keep the
subprocess path. This is the one place the design doc expects an
upstream-friendly patch.
close_reason: Correlation bound via object store; flow and attention views shipped

title: History view: bead-to-commit correlation
description:
The History view: bead-to-commit correlation with a timeline.

**Scope**

- Commit table with confidence badges per link
- Timeline panel (`t` in bv) drawn on a Canvas, synced with the table
- Causality markers and causal-chain drill-down
- File-centric mode: file -> beads that touched it, with Quick Look on diffs
- Hotspots and orphan-commit tabs
- Confirm/reject feedback, which adjusts future confidence

Depends on the correlation engine binding.
close_reason: History view shipped with timeline, causality, files, hotspots, orphans and feedback

title: Time-travel mode with diff badges
description:
Load bead state as of an arbitrary git revision and diff it against now.

**Scope**

- Revision scrubber in the toolbar over recent commits
- Per-issue diff badges: `NEW`, `CLOSED`, `MODIFIED`, `REOPENED`
- Time-travel summary panel
- Engine methods `snapshot_at` and `diff`

bv auto-emits JSON for `--diff-since` when stdout is not a TTY; the resolved
revision is echoed in the payload, and bvx should surface the same resolved
revision rather than the user's raw input.
close_reason: Time travel with revision scrubber and per-bead diff badges

title: Sprint dashboard with burndown
description:
Sprint dashboard with a burndown chart.

**Scope**

- Burndown line with an ideal-line overlay (Swift Charts)
- Velocity comparison chart
- At-risk detection banner
- Engine methods `burndown`, `sprint_list`, `sprint_show`, `capacity`

The `Sprint` model already exists in `BVXCore` but nothing reads it yet.
close_reason: Sprint dashboard with burndown, velocity, at-risk banner and capacity

title: Flow matrix and attention views
description:
Two label-scoped analytics views. The engine already exposes `label_flow`, so
this is largely presentation.

**Flow matrix** — cross-label dependency heat map with a bottleneck-score colour
scale; clicking a cell filters the list to those edges. Drilldown mode shows the
individual dependencies behind a cell.

**Attention view** — labels ranked by attention score, with the score
decomposition shown in the inspector rather than only the ranking.
close_reason: Correlation bound via object store; flow and attention views shipped

title: Recipe system for declarative views
description:
Declarative view configuration, as in bv's `.beads/recipes/*.yaml`.

**Scope**

- Load built-in and user recipes (engine method `recipes` exists)
- Sidebar section listing them
- Applying a recipe sets filter, sort and view atomically
- A form-based editor for user recipes

Built-ins worth having on day one: `actionable`, `high-impact`.
close_reason: Recipe system with sidebar, atomic apply and form editor

title: Static site export wizard
description:
Static site export: a shareable dashboard bundle.

**Scope**

- Native multi-step wizard sheet replacing bv's `huh` TUI flow
- SQLite payload plus the interactive graph
- Optional Rust/WASM hybrid search scorer
- Deploy targets (GitHub Pages, Cloudflare), with credentials in the **Keychain**
  rather than environment variables

`pkg/export` is already linked into the archive for the Markdown report, so the
Go side is largely reachable already.
close_reason: Static site export wizard with in-process GitHub Pages deploy and Keychain credentials

title: Multi-repository workspace support
description:
Multi-repository workspaces via `.bv/workspace.yaml`.

**Scope**

- Aggregate loader across repos (`pkg/workspace` is public)
- ID namespacing by prefix, with prefix badges on rows
- Cross-repository dependency edges, styled distinctly in the graph
- Repo picker in the sidebar (bv binds `w`)
- Per-repo filtering

Note `Issue.sourceRepo` already exists in the model and is decoded, but nothing
populates or displays it yet.
close_reason: Multi-repo workspaces with picker, prefix badges, cross-repo edges and filtering

title: Semantic and hybrid search modes
description:
Semantic and hybrid search modes alongside the existing fuzzy search.

**Scope**

- Scope bar toggling fuzzy / semantic
- Hybrid weights popover with live re-ranking
- Engine method `search` with mode, preset and weights

**Parity caveat**

bv defaults to a `hash` embedder. An on-device Core ML embedder would give
better results but *changes ranking*, so it must be opt-in and clearly labelled
— the default has to keep matching the CLI.
close_reason: Hybrid search with scope bar, presets, live weights and score breakdown

title: Complete robot protocol parity in bvx-cli
description:
Complete `bvx-cli`'s robot-protocol coverage.

Today it exposes a useful subset (`triage`, `plan`, `metrics`, `impact`,
`label-health`, `unblocks`, `blocker-chain`, `eta`, `export-md`, `doctor`) but
not the full ~45 flags, and it does not emit TOON.

**Scope**

- Remaining `--robot-*` commands
- TOON output format
- A parity harness diffing `bvx-cli --robot-X` against `bv --robot-X` across the
  fixture corpus, with an enumerated exception list (timing fields, absolute
  paths, version strings)

The parity harness is the point: it is what turns "same functionality" into a
checked claim rather than an assertion.
close_reason: Robot protocol, TOON encoder and a parity harness that verifies agreement with bv

title: Alerts panel and drift detection
description:
Alerts panel: proactive health warnings.

**Scope**

- Severity-grouped list (bv binds `!`)
- Filter by severity, type and label
- Optional `UNUserNotificationCenter` delivery for critical alerts while watching
- Baseline save/show and drift check, feeding the same panel

Engine methods `alerts` and `drift` are already reachable through `rawJSON`.
close_reason: Alerts panel with severity grouping, filters, baselines, drift and notifications

title: App Intents, URL scheme and Spotlight
description:
Native automation surfaces, over and above the CLI.

**Scope**

- App Intents / Shortcuts actions: `GetTriage`, `GetNextBead`,
  `GetExecutionPlan`, `GetAlerts`, `ForecastBead`, `ExportReport`
- `bvx://open?workspace=…&bead=…&view=graph` URL scheme (the scheme is already
  declared in `Info.plist` but nothing handles it)
- Spotlight indexing via `CSSearchableIndex`, so a bead id typed into Spotlight
  opens it in bvx
- "Install Command Line Tool…" menu item symlinking the bundled `bvx-cli`
close_reason: App Intents, bvx:// URL scheme, Spotlight indexing and CLI installer

title: Interactive tutorial
description:
Interactive tutorial, as bv offers on `` ` ``.

**Scope**

- Separate `WindowGroup` with persisted progress
- Sections mirroring bv's
- Context-sensitive "learn this view" links from each surface

Lowest priority of the parity gaps: the app is discoverable through its menu bar
and command palette in a way the TUI is not, so this buys less here than it does
in bv.
close_reason: Interactive tutorial with persisted progress and per-surface links

title: Markdown tables are not rendered in the description
description:
`MarkdownParser` has no table support, so a pipe table in a description is
mangled. Verified against the real parser:

```
input:  | Metric | Value |
        |---|---|
        | PageRank | 0.20 |

parsed: paragraph("| Metric | Value | |---|---| | PageRank | 0.20 |")
```

Two distinct symptoms depending on the rest of the text:

- **Table alone** — `looksLikeMarkdown` returns `false`, so the description
  renders verbatim. Rows survive but show as literal pipes in body font.
- **Table beside any other Markdown** — detection fires, the rows fall through
  to the paragraph branch, and `joinSoftWrapped` collapses every row onto a
  single line. This is the bad one, and it is a side effect of the soft-break
  fix: correct for prose, destructive for tables.

**Scope**

- `MarkdownBlock.table(headers:rows:alignments:)`
- Recognise a header row followed by a delimiter row (`|---|:--:|---:|`),
  including the leading/trailing-pipe-optional forms
- Render with SwiftUI `Grid`, honouring column alignment, inline spans per cell,
  and horizontal scroll when the table is wider than the inspector
- Add `|` as a detection signal *only* when a delimiter row follows, so prose
  containing a stray pipe is not misread

**Tests**

Parser cases for aligned/unaligned, ragged rows (fewer cells than headers),
tables with inline code in cells, and a false-positive guard for prose like
`use a | b to pipe`. Plus a render snapshot.
close_reason: Markdown tables parse and render; regression tests added

title: Make bead ids in the detail view clickable
description:
In the detail pane, a bead id mentioned in prose should be clickable and select
that bead.

Today the **Dependencies** section links beads, but an id inside the
description, notes or a comment is inert text. Descriptions routinely say things
like "work on bvx-8ou first to unblock this", and following that reference means
finding it manually in the list.

**Scope**

- Detect ids matching the workspace prefix plus `br`'s minted token
  (`bvx-8ou`, `bvx-v49`, and the longer forms), taken from the store's
  configured `issue_prefix` rather than hardcoded
- Render each as a link that sets `store.selection`
- Apply in the description, and in comment bodies
- **Only link ids that exist in the loaded workspace.** An unknown or stale id
  stays plain text — a link that selects nothing is worse than no link
- Show the target's title on hover

**Design note**

This interacts with the Markdown work: linkification has to run on the inline
span *after* `AttributedString` parsing, or it will corrupt ids that appear
inside fenced code and inline code, where they must stay literal.
close_reason: Bead ids in descriptions and comments link to their bead

title: Sort the issue list from its column headers
description:
Sort the issue list by clicking its column headers, the way every native macOS
table does, instead of only through the toolbar's Sort dropdown.

**Scope**

- Move `IssueListView` to SwiftUI `Table`'s `sortOrder:` binding with
  `TableColumn(_, value:)`, which gives clickable headers and the direction
  chevron for free
- Keep the toolbar menu — it stays the discoverable path and is where
  non-column orderings live

**Two constraints that are easy to get wrong**

- **Metric columns must stay disabled until Phase 2 lands.** Sorting by PageRank
  before it is computed would order by absent values. The existing
  `hasPhase2Values` gate has to cover the header path too, not just the menu.
- **bv's `s` key cycles sort modes**, and the terminal-keys layer still binds it.
  Header clicks and the cycle must drive the same state, or the two disagree
  about what the current order is.

**Tests**

Header-driven ordering for each column, a metric column staying inert before
Phase 2, and agreement between the header state and `SortMode`.
close_reason: Column headers sort the list, sharing one sort state with the toolbar and the s cycle

title: Multi-selection in the issue list
description:
Let the list select more than one bead at a time, the way every native macOS
table does.

**Scope**

- Move `store.selection` from `Issue.ID?` to `Set<Issue.ID>`, which is what
  SwiftUI `Table`'s `selection:` binding takes for multi-select
- Shift-click for a range, Command-click to add or remove one

**What the change ripples into**

`selection` is read in a lot of places that assume exactly one bead, and each
needs a decision rather than a mechanical fix:

- **The inspector** shows one bead. With several selected it should show the
  most recently added one or a summary of the set — showing the first silently
  hides that more are selected.
- **`selectedIssue` and `select(id:)`** are single-bead helpers used by the
  inline bead-id links, the `bvx://` URL scheme, Spotlight activation, the flow
  matrix drilldown, the alerts panel and the sprint critical path. All of those
  should still end up with exactly one bead selected — replacing the selection
  rather than extending it.
- **bv's `j`/`k` bindings** move a single cursor. They should keep doing that,
  which means the terminal-keys layer needs a notion of "the focused bead"
  distinct from "the selected set".

**Tests**

A shift-click range, that `select(id:)` replaces rather than extends, that the
inspector does something defensible with two selected, and that `j`/`k` still
move one cursor.
close_reason: Implemented: multi-selection with a derived focus, a selection-sensitive context menu with Copy ID, and an Open-panel guard backed by the new bvx_probe entry point

title: Context menu on the issue list, starting with Copy ID
description:
Right-clicking a row should offer actions, and those actions should know how
many beads they apply to.

**Scope**

- `.contextMenu(forSelectionType: Issue.ID.self)` on the `Table`. This is the
  API that matches the requirement exactly: SwiftUI hands the closure the set
  the menu applies to — the current selection when the right-clicked row is
  part of it, otherwise just that row. So "the selected beads, or the hovered
  one when it is not in the selection" falls out of the framework rather than
  having to be reconstructed from mouse position.
- First item: **Copy ID**. One bead copies its id; several copy the ids joined
  with `", "`.
- Build the menu so it can carry more items later, with distinct zero-, one-
  and many-selection variants from the start.

**Watch out**

- **The empty case is real.** Right-clicking the table's background yields an
  empty set. The menu should degrade to workspace-level items, or to nothing —
  not to a Copy ID that puts an empty string on the clipboard.
- **Order the joined ids by what is on screen**, not by `Set` iteration, which
  is unordered. Otherwise copying the same selection twice can produce two
  different strings.

**Tests**

One selected, several selected — asserting both the `", "` separator and a
stable order — and the empty case putting nothing on the pasteboard.
close_reason: Implemented: multi-selection with a derived focus, a selection-sensitive context menu with Copy ID, and an Open-panel guard backed by the new bvx_probe entry point

title: Only offer folders that hold bead data in the open panel
description:
The Open panel accepts any folder, so a folder with no bead data fails only
after it has been chosen. `NSOpenPanel`'s delegate can disable the ones that
cannot work, making the mistake unavailable rather than reported.

**Scope**

- `NSOpenPanelDelegate.panel(_:shouldEnable:)`, returning false for a directory
  the engine could not open

**The rule is not simply "contains .beads"**

`resolveSource` accepts several shapes, and a naive check would disable things
that work today:

- a folder containing `.beads`
- a `.beads` directory chosen directly
- a `.jsonl` or `.db` file chosen directly
- **a multi-repository workspace root**, which holds `.bv/workspace.yaml` while
  its `.beads` directories live in the repositories *below* it. Requiring
  `.beads` at the chosen level would make every workspace root unselectable.
  This is the case most likely to be missed, and it would silently undo
  bvx-e3y.
- a folder *below* one containing `.beads`, since discovery walks upwards

**Keep one copy of the rule**

Whatever predicate is written should be derived from the engine's discovery
rules rather than being a second implementation of them in Swift. Two copies
will drift, and the symptom — a folder that the panel refuses but the CLI opens
happily — is confusing enough to be worth designing out.

**Tests**

Each accepted shape above enables; a folder with no bead data anywhere above or
below it does not; and a workspace root with `.bv/workspace.yaml` enables.
close_reason: Implemented: multi-selection with a derived focus, a selection-sensitive context menu with Copy ID, and an Open-panel guard backed by the new bvx_probe entry point
